key_insight: Reinforcement learning discovers quantum repeater protocols on non-linear networks that outperform a routed swap-ASAP baseline by searching beyond disjoint-path routing.
engineering_relevance: Quantum network control architectures may benefit from supporting non-routing operations rather than restricting entanglement distribution to independent chains.
method: Apply reinforcement learning to protocol design on non-linear quantum repeater networks.
Optimize over a broader protocol space than disjoint-path entanglement routing allows.
Compare learned protocols with a routed extension of swap-ASAP.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improved performance over routed swap-ASAP even in parameter regimes where that baseline is considered state of the art, but provides no numerical gains or evaluation scale.
watch_item: Scalability remains a concern because the protocol search space grows exponentially with network size.
paper_title: Reinforcement Learning designs Quantum Repeater Protocols on Networks beyond the Chain Scenario
